records.literal_gloss: When therefore knew the Jesus that heard the Pharisees that Jesus more disciples makes and baptizes than John \v 2 (although indeed Jesus himself not was baptizing, but the disciples of him), \v 3 he left the Judea and went away again into the Galilee.

en.L: So when Jesus knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John \v 2 (although Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was not baptizing, but {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples [were]), \v 3 {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left Judea and went away again into Galilee.
en.B: Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was making and baptizing more disciples than John. \v 2 (In fact it was not Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} who baptized, but {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.) \v 3 So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left Judea and went back once more to Galilee.
en.R: The Pharisees heard that more people were becoming Jesus's disciples than John's, and that Jesus was baptizing them. Jesus knew that they had heard this. \v 2 (Really it was Jesus's disciples who did the baptizing, not Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.) \v 3 So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left Judea and went back to Galilee.

ko.L: 그러므로 바리새파 사람들이, 예수께서 요한보다 더 많은 제자를 만들고 세례를 주신다는 말을 들었다는 것을 예수께서 아셨을 때 \v 2 (그러나 예수께서 친히 세례를 주신 것이 아니라 그분의 제자들이 [준 것이었다]) \v 3 그분은 유대를 떠나 다시 갈릴리로 가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는, 자신이 요한보다 더 많은 사람을 제자로 삼고 세례를 주신다는 소식을 바리새파 사람들이 들었다는 것을 아셨다. \v 2 (사실 세례는 예수께서 친히 주신 것이 아니라 그분의 제자들이 준 것이었다.) \v 3 그래서 예수께서는 유대를 떠나 다시 갈릴리로 돌아가셨다.
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들은 요한보다 예수의 제자가 되는 사람이 더 많고, 예수께서 그들에게 세례를 주신다는 말을 들었다. 예수께서는 그들이 이 말을 들은 것을 아셨다. \v 2 (사실은 예수께서 직접 세례를 주신 것이 아니라 예수의 제자들이 세례를 주었다.) \v 3 그래서 예수께서는 유대를 떠나 갈릴리로 돌아가셨다.

vi.L: Vậy, khi Đức Giê-xu biết rằng người Pha-ri-si đã nghe rằng Đức Giê-xu thu nhận và làm báp-têm cho nhiều môn đồ hơn Giăng \v 2 (dù chính Đức Giê-xu không làm báp-têm, nhưng [là] các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}), \v 3 {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời Giu-đê và lại đi về Ga-li-lê.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu biết rằng người Pha-ri-si đã nghe tin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thu nhận và làm báp-têm cho nhiều môn đồ hơn Giăng. \v 2 (Thật ra không phải chính Đức Giê-xu làm báp-têm, mà là các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.) \v 3 Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời Giu-đê và trở lại Ga-li-lê một lần nữa.
vi.R: Người Pha-ri-si nghe tin rằng số người theo làm môn đồ Đức Giê-xu đông hơn số môn đồ của Giăng, và Đức Giê-xu làm báp-têm cho họ. Đức Giê-xu biết họ đã nghe tin ấy. \v 2 (Thật ra, các môn đồ của Đức Giê-xu làm báp-têm, chứ không phải chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.) \v 3 Vì thế, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời Giu-đê, trở về Ga-li-lê.

decisions.choice: Jesus (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, among them some of the oldest, read "the Lord" at the start of the verse; others, including Codex Sinaiticus, read "Jesus", and the SBLGNT follows them. Both name the same person. Before the resurrection John's narrative seldom calls Jesus "the Lord" (6:23; 11:2), and the name comes twice more in these verses, which may have led copyists to vary it one way or the other. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus came to know what the Pharisees had heard; the second "Jesus" belongs to the report they heard
alternatives: Jesus knew it by his own insight (compare 2:25)
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to know or to come to know. The sentence stacks two "that" clauses: Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making more disciples than John. Repeating the name in the second clause shows it is what the Pharisees were told. John has already told how people were going to Jesus rather than to John (3:26).

decisions.choice: an aside correcting the report: Jesus's disciples did the baptizing, not Jesus himself
alternatives: Jesus baptized at first and later stopped
decisions.reason: In 3:22 and 3:26 Jesus is said to baptize. The narrator now adds that the baptizing was done by his disciples, under his authority, so the report is true in substance but not in the letter. The aside also keeps Jesus out of a contest of numbers with John (3:26-30): Jesus is the one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit (1:33). The words are in the manuscripts generally.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: a movement of teachers devoted to keeping the law strictly
decisions.reason: Pharisees were among those who questioned John the Baptist (1:24). Their interest in the growing movement around Jesus is the reason given for his leaving: the sentence makes the departure follow from what they had heard. John does not say what Jesus wished to avoid; later the authorities look for a way to kill him, but his hour has not yet come (5:18; 7:1, 30).

decisions.choice: learned (B); knew that they had heard this (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "learned" because the verb here means coming to know (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "knew", which can carry the same sense.

decisions.choice: the long sentence split, with verse 2 in parentheses
decisions.reason: The Greek is one sentence with an aside in the middle. Balanced and Readable break it into three and mark the aside with parentheses so that the main line, he left Judea, stays clear.

decisions.choice: more people were becoming Jesus's disciples than John's
decisions.reason: "Making disciples" means gaining followers who learn from a teacher; Readable says it plainly and keeps the word "disciples", as everywhere in John.

decisions.choice: se enteró (B); supo (L, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the verb here means coming to know (meaning decision m2). "Supo" in the pretérito already has that sense in Spanish.

decisions.choice: the long sentence split, with verse 2 in parentheses
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable break the sentence and mark the aside, so the main line, he left Judea, stays clear.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; "친히", "그분" and the honorific "-시-" carry the respect
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span around "그분" (it would have nothing to change)
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change and the Korean text has no such spans, here or anywhere in this passage. Respect for Jesus is carried at every level by "께서", the honorific "-시-" and "그분".

decisions.choice: "thu nhận và làm báp-têm cho nhiều môn đồ" (receives and baptizes more disciples)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "làm môn đồ" would mean "becomes a disciple"; "thu nhận" says that Jesus is the one gaining them. "làm báp-têm" is the established Protestant term for baptize.

source.text: ἔδει δὲ αὐτὸν διέρχεσθαι διὰ τῆς Σαμαρείας.

records.literal_gloss: It was necessary now [for] him to pass through the Samaria.

en.L: Now it was necessary for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to pass through Samaria.
en.B: He had to pass through Samaria.
en.R: Jesus had to go through Samaria.

es.L: Y era necesario que pasara por Samaria.
es.B: Tenía que pasar por Samaria.
es.R: Jesús tenía que pasar por Samaria.

sw.L: Basi ilimlazimu kupita katikati ya Samaria.
sw.B: Ilimpasa apite katikati ya Samaria.
sw.R: Yesu alilazimika kupita Samaria.

ko.L: 그런데 그분은 사마리아를 거쳐 지나가셔야 했다.
ko.B: 그분은 사마리아를 거쳐 가셔야 했다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 사마리아를 지나가셔야 했다.

vi.L: Bấy giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cần phải đi ngang qua Sa-ma-ri.
vi.B: Ngài phải đi qua Sa-ma-ri.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu phải đi qua vùng Sa-ma-ri.

decisions.choice: had to: a necessity John leaves open; the route required it, and in John "must" also marks what God has planned
alternatives: only the road: the shortest way ran through Samaria
only God's plan: he was sent to this town
decisions.reason: Travelers going north from Judea could go straight through Samaria or go around it by the Jordan valley. Josephus says the road through Samaria took three days and was the one Galileans used on their way to the festivals (Life 269; Antiquities 20.118), so the road alone could explain it. But John uses this verb, ἔδει, for what God's purpose requires: the Son of Man must be lifted up (3:14), he must increase (3:30), he must bring other sheep (10:16). What happens at the well suggests the second sense is present too. The evidence is balanced, so every level says only "had to" and makes neither sense explicit.

decisions.choice: Samaria: the region between Judea and Galilee, home of the Samaritans
decisions.reason: Samaria was first the capital, then the name, of the northern kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 16:24). In Jesus's day it was the land of the Samaritans, who worshiped the God of Israel but were divided from the Jews (verse 9).

decisions.choice: it was necessary (L); had to (B, R)
decisions.reason: Plain words that keep both senses of the necessity open (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus at the start of the journey.

decisions.choice: era necesario (L); tenía que (B, R)
decisions.reason: Plain words that keep both senses of the necessity open (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἔρχεται οὖν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας λεγομένην Συχὰρ πλησίον τοῦ χωρίου ὃ ἔδωκεν Ἰακὼβ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: He comes therefore to a city of the Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that gave Jacob to the Joseph the son of him;

en.L: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob gave to Joseph his son.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to a Samaritan town called Sychar, near the piece of land that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
en.R: He came to a town in Samaria called Sychar. It was near the field that Jacob had given to his son Joseph long ago.

ko.L: 그래서 그분은 야곱이 자기 아들 요셉에게 준 땅 가까이, 수가라고 하는 사마리아의 한 마을로 오신다.

vi.L: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến một thành của Sa-ma-ri gọi là Si-kha, gần thửa đất mà Gia-cốp đã cho Giô-sép, con mình.
vi.B: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến một thành của người Sa-ma-ri tên là Si-kha, gần mảnh đất Gia-cốp đã cho con trai mình là Giô-sép.
vi.R: Ngài đến một thành trong vùng Sa-ma-ri tên là Si-kha. Thành ấy ở gần cánh đồng mà ngày xưa Gia-cốp đã cho con trai mình là Giô-sép.

decisions.choice: Sychar: a town near Shechem whose exact site is not certain
decisions.reason: Only John mentions Sychar. It is usually placed at the village of Askar, a short walk north of the well shown today as Jacob's well, at the foot of Mount Gerizim; others take it to be ancient Shechem, whose ruins lie close to the well. Either way it was near enough for the woman to come from it for water (verses 7, 28).

decisions.choice: the land Jacob gave to Joseph at Shechem
decisions.reason: Jacob bought a plot of ground at Shechem (Genesis 33:18-19), and on his deathbed gave Joseph one portion more than his brothers (Genesis 48:22, where the Hebrew word for "portion" is the same as the name Shechem). Joseph's bones were buried there (Joshua 24:32). The Samaritans, who claimed descent from Joseph, lived in the middle of this history (verse 12).

decisions.choice: town: a settlement with its own community, large or small
decisions.reason: The word is used of any town or village with its own people and life; Sychar was small.

decisions.choice: town
decisions.reason: "City" suggests a large place; this was a country town.

decisions.choice: came
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("he comes", "she says") for vividness. Here and through the rest of the passage Balanced and Readable use the past, normal for a story told in this language; Literal keeps the present.

decisions.choice: long ago
decisions.reason: Readable shows that Jacob lived many centuries before.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("llega", "le dice"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: pueblo
decisions.reason: As in English: "ciudad" suggests a large place; Sicar was a small town (meaning decision m3). Literal uses the same word, as in 1:44.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anafika); past at Balanced and Readable (alifika)
decisions.reason: As in John 1: Literal keeps the Greek present of past events; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, as written Swahili does. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("오신다", "말씀하신다", "말한다"); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: John tells much of this scene in the present tense. Literal keeps it, as the guide asks; Balanced and Readable use the past, which is how Korean narrative is told. One decision for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "마을" for the town
decisions.reason: "도시" suggests a city; Sychar was a small settlement, and "마을" is the plain word for it.

decisions.choice: historic present: Literal "đến" without "đã"; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past where Vietnamese needs it
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not change for tense, so John's historic present shows only in Literal leaving out "đã" and in plain sequence words; one decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: "thành"
decisions.reason: "thành" covers a settlement of any size; "thành phố" would suggest a modern city.

source.text: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πηγὴ τοῦ Ἰακώβ.

records.literal_gloss: Was now there [the] spring of the Jacob.

en.L: Now the spring of Jacob was there.
en.B: Jacob's well was there.
en.R: Jacob's well was there.

es.L: Y estaba allí la fuente de Jacob.
es.B: Allí estaba el pozo de Jacob.
es.R: Allí estaba el pozo de Jacob.

sw.L: Basi chemchemi ya Yakobo ilikuwa huko.
sw.B: Kisima cha Yakobo kilikuwa hapo.
sw.R: Kisima cha Yakobo kilikuwa hapo.

ko.L: 그런데 거기에 야곱의 샘이 있었다.
ko.B: 그곳에는 야곱의 우물이 있었다.
ko.R: 거기에 야곱의 우물이 있었다.

vi.L: Ở đó có mạch nước của Gia-cốp.
vi.B: Ở đó có giếng Gia-cốp.
vi.R: Ở đó có giếng Gia-cốp.

decisions.choice: spring: a source of water; here a deep well that reaches spring water
alternatives: a spring flowing at the surface
decisions.reason: The narrator calls it πηγὴ, a spring or source; the woman calls it φρέαρ, a well dug down into the ground (verses 11-12). Both fit a deep well fed by groundwater. The narrator's word prepares for verse 14, where Jesus promises a spring of water within a person.

decisions.choice: Jacob's well: a well tied to Jacob by tradition
decisions.reason: The Old Testament does not tell of Jacob digging a well; the name comes from tradition linked with the land he owned here (verse 5). The woman speaks of Jacob as the one who gave the well (verse 12). A deep well at the foot of Mount Gerizim, near modern Nablus, has been shown as Jacob's well since early Christian times.

decisions.choice: well
decisions.reason: In ordinary speech this is a well, the word the woman uses. Literal keeps "spring" so the link with verse 14 can be seen; there every level says "spring".

decisions.choice: fuente (L); pozo (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: in ordinary speech this is a well, the word the woman uses. Literal keeps "fuente" so the link with verse 14 can be seen; there every level says "fuente" or "manantial".

source.text: ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς κεκοπιακὼς ἐκ τῆς ὁδοιπορίας ἐκαθέζετο οὕτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ· ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Jesus, having become weary from the journey, was sitting thus at the spring; [the] hour was about [the] sixth.

en.L: So Jesus, worn out from the journey, was sitting thus at the spring; [the] hour was about [the] sixth.
en.B: Jesus was worn out from the journey, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down by the well just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. It was about noon.
en.R: Jesus was tired from the long walk, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down by the well. It was about noon.

es.L: Jesús, pues, cansado del camino, estaba sentado así junto a la fuente; era como la hora sexta.

ko.L: 그래서 예수께서는 길을 걸어오느라 지치셔서 그대로 샘 곁에 앉아 계셨다. 여섯째 시쯤이었다.

decisions.choice: worn out from the journey: Jesus is truly tired
decisions.reason: The verb is used of being tired out by hard work or travel. The Word who became flesh (1:14) is weary here and thirsty (verse 7), as he weeps at 11:35 and thirsts on the cross (19:28).

decisions.choice: thus: just as he was, tired, without more ado
alternatives: on the ground by the well
decisions.reason: The adverb points back to his tiredness: worn out as he was, he simply sat down there. It adds no further fact.

decisions.choice: the sixth hour: about noon
alternatives: about six in the morning or evening, counting the hours from midnight
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise, about six in the morning (see the note at 1:39), so the sixth hour was midday, the heat of the day. Counting from midnight, which some have proposed for John, would give six in the morning or evening. Genesis 24:11 speaks of evening as the time women went out to draw water; John does not say why this woman came at noon. The same hour is named at 19:14, when Pilate brings Jesus out to the crowd.

decisions.choice: was sitting: the scene is set when the woman arrives
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes him seated at the well as the next event happens.

decisions.choice: about noon
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: clock times stay literal at Literal, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: worn out from the journey (L, B); tired from the long walk (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for being tired out by travel.

decisions.choice: just as he was
decisions.reason: Gives the sense of the adverb (meaning decision m2); Readable leaves it in "so".

decisions.choice: cerca del mediodía
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: clock times stay literal at Literal, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: saa sita at every level; mchana added at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in 1:39: the Greek counts hours from sunrise, as Swahili time does, so "the sixth hour" is "saa sita", which is noon in Swahili time. No level needs to convert it. Balanced and Readable add "mchana" (in the day).

decisions.choice: from Samaria: a woman of the region and its people, a Samaritan
decisions.reason: The old city of Samaria, rebuilt by Herod as Sebaste, lay too far off for her to come here for water. The phrase names her people; verse 9 calls her "the Samaritan woman", and she comes from the nearby town (verse 28).

decisions.choice: a meeting at a well, which in Scripture often leads to a betrothal
decisions.reason: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah at a well (Genesis 24:10-27); Jacob meets Rachel at a well (Genesis 29:1-12); Moses meets Zipporah at a well (Exodus 2:15-21). Here, at Jacob's well, a stranger asks a woman for water, and the talk turns to her husbands (verses 16-18); John the Baptist has just called Jesus the bridegroom (3:29). John does not draw the link himself, so every level tells the meeting plainly.

decisions.choice: a request that crosses two lines of custom
decisions.reason: A Jewish man asks a Samaritan woman he does not know for water, and would drink from her vessel. The woman is surprised (verse 9), and so are the disciples later (verse 27). Jesus begins with his own need.

decisions.choice: a request in the form of a command
decisions.reason: The command form was the ordinary way to ask for something; it is not rude.

decisions.choice: Will you give me a drink?
decisions.reason: A bare command can sound rude to young readers; the question keeps it a request (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Dame de beber (L, B); ¿Me das de beber? (R)
decisions.reason: "Dame de beber" is the ordinary way to ask for a drink in Spanish and is not rude (meaning decision m2). Readable makes it a question, as the English does, so young readers hear a request.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체: "다오", "-느냐", "-라") throughout the conversation
decisions.reason: As the guide sets for the whole book: Jesus speaks to the people he meets in 해라체, and Readable softens the words, not the speech level. Narration gives Jesus the honorific "께서 ... -시-".

decisions.choice: forms of address in 4:7-26: Jesus says "Ta" for himself and "chị" to the woman; she says "tôi" and calls him "ông"; the narrator calls her "chị ấy"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must name the relation. "chị" is respectful and warm toward a woman of uncertain age; she, meeting a Jewish stranger, uses the polite "ông". Kept through the scene so the relationship does not shift.

decisions.choice: a Jew: a member of the Jewish people
decisions.reason: She recognizes him as one of the Jewish people, perhaps by his speech or dress. Jesus is a Jew, and in verse 22 he counts himself among them ("we").

decisions.choice: Jews and Samaritans: two peoples long divided
decisions.reason: The Samaritans worshiped the God of Israel and kept the five books of Moses, but had their own temple on Mount Gerizim (verse 20). Jewish tradition traced them to the peoples the Assyrians settled in the land (2 Kings 17:24-41). The Jewish ruler John Hyrcanus destroyed the Gerizim temple late in the second century BC (Josephus, Antiquities 13.255-256), and the hostility between the two peoples ran deep (Luke 9:52-53).

decisions.choice: two barriers: Jew and Samaritan, man and woman
decisions.reason: The two participles set what he is against what she is, and she names herself a woman as well as a Samaritan. Verse 27 shows that a man talking with a woman in public also surprised the disciples.

decisions.choice: two statements, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the two facts first, so that the reason for her surprise is clear.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}
decisions.reason: The stressed "tú" for Christ takes the setting; at the start of a sentence (Readable) it is written plain. "A mí" is the woman.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks to Jesus in 합쇼체 ("-십니까", "-습니다"); "you" is "선생님" or left out, never "당신"
decisions.reason: People who address Jesus use 합쇼체 throughout the book. A Korean speaker does not call a stranger "당신" politely, so the Greek "you" is left to the honorific verb or given as "선생님", in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: "ông" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English marks her "you" with the setting. In Vietnamese she addresses a stranger as "ông", a noun of address that is not capitalised for reverence; she does not yet know who he is.

decisions.choice: do not use things in common with: they do not share vessels
alternatives: have no dealings with, do not associate with
decisions.reason: The verb συγχρῶνται is rare. Formed from "with" and "use", it can mean to use something together with someone, and more broadly to have dealings with them. The broad sense sits awkwardly with verse 8, where the disciples go to buy food in a Samaritan town. The narrow sense suits the scene: Jesus has no vessel (verse 11) and would drink from hers, and a later Jewish ruling treated Samaritan women as always unclean, and so what they handled (Mishnah Niddah 4:1). The broader sense remains possible and is widely known; the footnote gives it.

decisions.choice: the narrator's comment, not the woman's words
decisions.reason: The sentence explains a custom for readers who did not know it, as John explains other Jewish customs (2:6). It stands outside her words.

decisions.choice: Jews: the Jewish people
decisions.reason: The word means the people as a whole, set beside the Samaritans as a people.

decisions.choice: the sentence is part of the text (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the sentence is missing (the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts)
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts leave the sentence out, perhaps because it seemed to contradict verse 8; the great majority have it. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: in parentheses
decisions.reason: Marks the sentence as the narrator's aside (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: use [things] in common (L); use the same vessels (B); share a cup or a bowl (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the shape of the verb; Balanced and Readable name what was not shared (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Jews
decisions.reason: The word means the people here, so every level says "Jews" (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: usan [cosas] en común (L); los mismos recipientes (B); vasos ni platos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the shape of the verb; Balanced and Readable name what was not shared (meaning decision m1), in parentheses as the narrator's aside.

en.B: Jesus answered her, "If you knew the gift God gives, and who it is that says to you, 'Give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a drink,' it is you who would have asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would have given you living water."
en.R: Jesus answered, "You do not know what God wants to give you. And you do not know who is asking you for a drink. If you did, you would have asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for water, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would have given you living water."

decisions.choice: an unreal condition with the roles reversed
decisions.reason: She does not know, and so she has not asked. The "you" in "you would have asked" is emphatic (σὺ): he asked her for water, but she is the one who should be asking him.

decisions.choice: the gift of God: what God freely gives, which the sentence names as living water
decisions.reason: δωρεὰν means a free gift. The sentence links God's gift with the living water Jesus would give; in 7:37-39 John explains living water as the Spirit, and in 3:16 God gives his Son. These belong together, so every level says only God's gift.

decisions.choice: living water: both fresh flowing water and water that gives life
alternatives: only a picture of eternal life
decisions.reason: In everyday speech living water was fresh water running from a spring or stream, as against still water in a cistern (Genesis 26:19; Leviticus 14:5, 50). Scripture also calls the LORD "the spring of living water" (Jeremiah 2:13; 17:13), and the prophets see living water flowing out from Jerusalem (Zechariah 14:8; Ezekiel 47:1-12). Jesus means the water of life that he gives; the woman hears the everyday sense (verse 11). The double meaning is deliberate, so every level keeps "living water".

decisions.choice: who it is: Jesus speaks of himself in the third person
decisions.reason: He points her to the question of who he is, which the conversation answers step by step: a Jew (verse 9), greater than Jacob (verse 12), a prophet (verse 19), the Messiah (verse 26).

decisions.choice: the gift God gives (B); what God wants to give you (R)
decisions.reason: Plain wording that keeps the gift open (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: it is you who would have asked him
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic "you" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: two statements, then the condition
decisions.reason: Readable states what she does not know before saying what would follow if she did.

decisions.choice: serías tú la que le pediría
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the emphatic "you" (meaning decision m1). This "tú" is the woman and has no setting; "a él" and "él" are Jesus.

decisions.choice: agua viva
decisions.reason: "Agua viva" keeps both senses, fresh running water and water that gives life (meaning decision m3), as the English "living water" does.

decisions.choice: maji yaliyo hai (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The meaning note keeps both senses: fresh, flowing water, and water that gives life. "Maji yaliyo hai" (water that is alive) can be heard both ways, which the woman's answer in verse 11 needs. "Maji ya uzima" (water of life) would give away the second sense too soon.

decisions.choice: "살아 있는 물" (L); "생수" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "생수" is everyday Korean for fresh spring water and is written with the characters for "living water", so it carries both senses of the Greek, as the meaning decision asks. Literal spells the phrase out word for word.

decisions.choice: "nước sống"
decisions.reason: "nước sống" can be heard as fresh water and as water that gives life, so the woman's misunderstanding in 4:11 still works; "nước hằng sống" would give away the spiritual sense at once.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself in the third person; Vietnamese "Ngài" in his own mouth would sound like self-praise, and "người ấy" keeps the riddle.

decisions.choice: Sir: a polite address to a man she does not know
decisions.reason: Κύριε is the word later used of Jesus as Lord (20:28), but it was also the ordinary courteous way to address a man. She does not yet know who he is. As the talk goes on she sees him as a prophet (verse 19) and wonders if he is the Christ (verse 29).

decisions.choice: bucket: a vessel for drawing water
decisions.reason: The word means something to draw water with, such as a bucket let down on a rope. Jesus has none.

decisions.choice: she takes living water in the everyday sense
decisions.reason: She thinks of running water and sees that he cannot even reach the water in this well, let alone a better source. John often lets hearers take Jesus's words at the everyday level before their meaning is opened (3:4; 4:33; 6:52).

decisions.choice: well: a shaft dug down to water
decisions.reason: A different word from the "spring" of verse 6; see the note there.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: The woman uses the word as a polite address (meaning decision m1); "Lord" would put in her mouth a confession she has not yet made. The footnote gives "Lord", the other sense of the same Greek word.

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: Spanish "señor" is both the polite "sir" and "Lord", so it keeps the woman's word without making her confess what she does not yet know (meaning decision m1). Here it is capitalized only because it begins her speech; it is the polite address. The footnote says so.

decisions.choice: her speech continues into verse 12
decisions.reason: The woman's question in verse 12 is part of what she says, so the quotation closes there. (The English closes it at the end of this verse.)

decisions.choice: bwana, placed inside the sentence
decisions.reason: Κύριε here is a polite "sir" to a stranger, and Swahili says "bwana" for both "sir" and "Lord". At the start of a sentence it would need a capital and read as "Lord"; placed after the first phrase, as Swahili often places a form of address, it stays lowercase and reads as "sir". The same in verses 15, 19 and 49.

decisions.choice: "선생님" for kyrie from the woman
decisions.reason: She does not yet know who Jesus is, so her "kyrie" is the polite "선생님", as in English; the footnote gives "주님". The same holds for her later "선생님" in this passage.

decisions.choice: "Thưa ông"
decisions.reason: She does not yet know who Jesus is, so "kyrie" is the polite address to a man, as in docs/john-terms.md; disciples and believers say "Chúa".

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is framed to expect "no". John's readers know the answer is yes; the same irony returns when the crowd asks whether Jesus is greater than Abraham (8:53).

decisions.choice: our father Jacob: the Samaritans claimed descent from Jacob through Joseph
decisions.reason: Josephus reports that the Samaritans called themselves descendants of Joseph through Ephraim and Manasseh (Antiquities 11.341). The well that Jacob gave stands for that claim.

decisions.choice: livestock: flocks and herds
decisions.reason: The word covers the animals a household raised and kept.

decisions.choice: ancestor
decisions.reason: Jacob lived long before; "father" in this sense is not plain for young readers.

decisions.choice: the question first (B) or last (R), with Jacob's gift as its own sentence
decisions.reason: Breaks the long question so it reads naturally; Readable's "Do you think" keeps the expected answer no (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso ...?; ¿Crees que ...? (R)
decisions.reason: A question that expects the answer no (meaning decision m1). The "él" of these sentences is Jacob and has no setting.

decisions.choice: antepasado
decisions.reason: As in English: Jacob lived long before; "padre" in this sense is not plain for young readers.

decisions.choice: "우리 조상 야곱" at every level
decisions.reason: "우리 아버지" would be read in Korean as her own father; "조상" says what "father" means here, the forefather of her people. Literal keeps the word order of the question, with Jacob's deeds as a relative clause before his name.

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" (we, not including the hearer)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose; she speaks for the Samaritans, who claim Jacob as father, and leaves the Jewish stranger out.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Everyone|Every man}} (L); {{gender:All who|All men who}} (B); {{gender:Anyone|Any man}} (R)

decisions.reason: Inclusive by default, since men and women are meant; the traditional form is the alternative.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Todo el que", "todos los que" and "cualquiera" are already general in Spanish, so no setting is needed here or in verse 14, where "en su interior" takes the place of a pronoun.

decisions.choice: no gender spans in this chapter
decisions.reason: As in John 3: the English offers "every man" and "him" as traditional alternatives, but Swahili "kila", "mtu", "watu" and the verbs say nothing about sex, so the setting has nothing to change in verses 13-14, 23 or 28.

decisions.choice: no gender spans: "누구나", "누구든지", "그 사람"
decisions.reason: Korean "누구나" and "사람" already include men and women, and Korean needs no "he" or "him" for the drinker, so the English gender spans here and in the next verses have no Korean counterpart.

decisions.choice: "ai" and "người ấy" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "ai" (whoever) and "người ấy" (that person) already include men and women, so the gender setting has nothing to change here or in 4:14.

decisions.choice: never, ever: the strongest denial, with "for ever"
decisions.reason: Two negatives together (οὐ μὴ) make the strongest denial, and "into the age" adds "for ever". The thirst that ordinary water only puts off, this water ends.

decisions.choice: whoever drinks: a single drink
decisions.reason: The aorist subjunctive looks at one act of drinking, set against the repeated drinking of verse 13.

decisions.choice: the water Jesus gives: the life he gives, which John later links with the Spirit
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say here what the water is. In 7:37-39 he promises rivers of living water flowing from within the one who believes, and John explains that he meant the Spirit. Isaiah promised water for the thirsty and the Spirit poured out (Isaiah 44:3; 55:1). Here the water becomes a source inside the person, no longer drawn from outside.

decisions.choice: leaping up: water gushing up from a spring
decisions.reason: The verb ἁλλομένου is used elsewhere of people jumping or leaping (Acts 3:8; 14:10). Used of water, it pictures a spring gushing up with force: water that is alive.

decisions.choice: into eternal life: the water rises and issues in eternal life
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the direction and goal of the water: it leads to eternal life. The same phrase is used of the harvest gathered "for eternal life" in verse 36.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, which begins now
decisions.reason: In John eternal life is the life of God's coming age, given now to those who believe (3:15-16, 36; 5:24).

decisions.choice: leaping up (L); leaps up (B); bubble up (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is used of jumping (meaning decision m4); "leaping" keeps that lively picture, which the more familiar renderings soften. Readable uses the plain word for water rising from a spring.

decisions.choice: never, ever
decisions.reason: One phrase that carries both the double negative and "into the age" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.reason: Readable sets up the contrast with verse 13 before stating it.

decisions.choice: five husbands: John gives the fact without explaining it
alternatives: a sign of a sinful life
a picture of the five peoples settled in Samaria (2 Kings 17:24)
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say why she had had five husbands. Under the law a husband could end a marriage but a wife could not (Deuteronomy 24:1-4), and a woman could be widowed more than once, so the number alone does not show whose fault it was. John records no rebuke; what amazes her is that he knows (verse 29). Some have read the five husbands as a picture of the five peoples the Assyrians settled in Samaria with their gods (2 Kings 17:24, 29-31); John gives no sign of it.

decisions.reason: The Greek "for" gives the reason her words were right; "in fact" does the same in natural speech.

decisions.choice: a prophet: one through whom God speaks and who may know what is hidden
decisions.reason: Prophets were known for seeing what was hidden (1 Samuel 9:19-20; 2 Kings 5:26; compare Luke 7:39). There is no article, so she does not yet call him "the Prophet" (1:21; 6:14). The Samaritans accepted only the five books of Moses as Scripture and looked for the prophet like Moses whom God had promised (Deuteronomy 18:15-18); her words point that way (verse 25).

decisions.choice: "예언자"
decisions.reason: "예언자" is the current word that new readers understand; "선지자" is the older Protestant term and may be preferred by a reviewer. The guide does not settle it.

source.text: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ προσεκύνησαν· καὶ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐστὶν ὁ τόπος ὅπου προσκυνεῖν δεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: The fathers of us on the mountain this worshiped; and you say that in Jerusalem is the place where to worship it is necessary."

en.L: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you [Jews] say that in Jerusalem is the place where [people] must worship."
en.B: This mountain is where our ancestors worshiped; yet you Jews say that Jerusalem is the place where worship must be offered."
en.R: Our ancestors worshiped God here on this mountain. But you Jews say that people must worship in Jerusalem."

es.L: Nuestros padres adoraron en este monte, y {{plural_you:ustedes [los judíos] dicen|vosotros [los judíos] decís}} que en Jerusalén está el lugar donde se debe adorar».
es.B: Nuestros antepasados adoraron en este monte, pero {{plural_you:ustedes los judíos dicen|vosotros los judíos decís}} que el lugar donde se debe adorar es Jerusalén».
es.R: Nuestros antepasados adoraron a Dios aquí, en este monte. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes los judíos dicen|vosotros los judíos decís}} que hay que adorar en Jerusalén».

sw.L: Baba zetu waliabudu katika mlima huu, na ninyi [Wayahudi] mnasema kwamba Yerusalemu ndipo mahali ambapo [watu] wanapaswa kuabudu."
sw.B: Mlima huu ndipo mababu zetu walipoabudu; lakini ninyi Wayahudi mnasema kwamba Yerusalemu ndipo mahali ambapo ibada inapaswa kufanyika."
sw.R: Mababu zetu walimwabudu Mungu hapa juu ya mlima huu. Lakini ninyi Wayahudi mnasema kwamba watu wanapaswa kuabudu Yerusalemu."

ko.L: 우리 조상들은 이 산에서 예배하였는데, [유대인] 여러분은 예배해야 할 곳이 예루살렘에 있다고 말합니다."
ko.B: 우리 조상들은 이 산에서 예배했습니다. 그런데 여러분 유대인들은 예배드려야 할 곳이 예루살렘이라고 말합니다."
ko.R: 우리 조상들은 여기 이 산에서 하나님께 예배했습니다. 그런데 여러분 유대인들은 사람들이 예루살렘에서 예배해야 한다고 말합니다."

vi.L: Tổ phụ chúng tôi đã thờ phượng trên núi này, còn các ông [người Do Thái] nói rằng Giê-ru-sa-lem là nơi [người ta] phải thờ phượng."
vi.B: Tổ tiên chúng tôi đã thờ phượng trên núi này, nhưng người Do Thái các ông lại nói Giê-ru-sa-lem mới là nơi phải thờ phượng."
vi.R: Tổ tiên chúng tôi đã thờ phượng Đức Chúa Trời trên núi này. Nhưng người Do Thái các ông lại nói rằng phải thờ phượng ở Giê-ru-sa-lem."

decisions.choice: this mountain: Mount Gerizim, above the well
decisions.reason: Mount Gerizim rises over the valley where the well lies. Moses commanded the blessing to be spoken from Gerizim (Deuteronomy 11:29; 27:12), and in the Samaritan form of the five books of Moses the altar of Deuteronomy 27:4 is on Gerizim, where the Jewish text has Mount Ebal. The Samaritans' temple there was destroyed late in the second century BC (see verse 9), but they went on worshiping on the mountain.

decisions.choice: our fathers: the Samaritans' ancestors, back to the patriarchs
decisions.reason: Abraham and Jacob built altars near Shechem (Genesis 12:6-7; 33:18-20). She appeals to her people's long tradition.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the Jews
decisions.reason: She sets "our fathers" against "you" in the plural: the Jews, whose view she takes this Jewish prophet to share.

decisions.choice: must: a duty laid down by God
decisions.reason: The Jewish claim rested on the command to worship at the place God would choose (Deuteronomy 12:5-14), which Scripture names as Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 6:6; Psalm 78:68). Jesus answers in verse 24 with a different "must".

decisions.choice: a question put to a prophet
alternatives: only a way of changing the subject
decisions.reason: Having found a prophet, she raises the question that divided the two peoples. Whether she is also turning the talk away from her own life the text does not say.

decisions.choice: you [Jews] (L); you Jews (B, R)
decisions.reason: The plural "you" (meaning decision m3) needs a word to show it. It refers to the Jews as a people, so it does not take the setting for pronouns of Christ.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forebears; "ancestors" says so plainly.

decisions.choice: ustedes [los judíos] (L); ustedes los judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb shows the plural, but not who is meant (meaning decision m3), so every level names the Jews. The plural "you" takes the reader setting (ustedes / vosotros), as throughout the passage; it is not a pronoun for Christ.

decisions.choice: "여러분" for the plural "you"
decisions.reason: Speaking up to Jesus in 합쇼체, the woman cannot use "너희", and "당신들" sounds hostile; "여러분" is the polite plural.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πίστευέ μοι, γύναι, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὔτε ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ οὔτε ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις προσκυνήσετε τῷ πατρί.

records.literal_gloss: Says to her the Jesus, "Believe me, woman, that is coming an hour when neither on the mountain this nor in Jerusalem you will worship the Father.

en.L: Jesus says to her, "Believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Woman, that an hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you [all] worship the Father.
en.B: Jesus said to her, "Believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Woman: an hour is coming when your worship of the Father will not be on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem either.
en.R: Jesus said to her, "Dear woman, believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. A time is coming when you and your people will worship the Father, but not on this mountain, and not in Jerusalem either.

es.L: Jesús le dice: «Créeme, mujer, que viene una hora en que ni en este monte ni en Jerusalén {{plural_you:adorarán|adoraréis}} al Padre.
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Créeme, mujer: viene una hora en que {{plural_you:ustedes no adorarán|vosotros no adoraréis}} al Padre ni en este monte ni en Jerusalén.
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Créeme, mujer. Llega la hora en que {{plural_you:tú y tu pueblo adorarán|tú y tu pueblo adoraréis}} al Padre, pero no en este monte, y tampoco en Jerusalén.

sw.L: Yesu anamwambia, "Niamini, Mama, kwamba saa inakuja ambapo hamtamwabudu Baba katika mlima huu wala Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Niamini, Mama: saa inakuja ambapo ibada yenu kwa Baba haitakuwa katika mlima huu, wala Yerusalemu pia.
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Mama, niamini. Wakati unakuja ambapo wewe na watu wako mtamwabudu Baba, lakini si juu ya mlima huu, wala si Yerusalemu pia.

ko.L: 예수께서 그 여자에게 말씀하신다. "여자여, 나를 믿어라. 너희가 이 산에서도, 예루살렘에서도 아버지께 예배하지 않을 때가 온다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그 여자에게 말씀하셨다. "여인이여, 내 말을 믿어라. 너희가 아버지께 드리는 예배가 이 산에서도, 예루살렘에서도 드려지지 않을 때가 온다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그 여자에게 말씀하셨다. "부인, 내 말을 믿어라. 너와 네 동족이 아버지께 예배할 때가 온다. 그런데 그때에는 이 산에서도 아니고 예루살렘에서도 아니다.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với chị ấy: "Hãy tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, hỡi chị, rằng giờ đang đến, khi các người sẽ thờ phượng Cha không phải trên núi này, cũng không phải tại Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với chị ấy: "Này chị, hãy tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: giờ đang đến, khi dân chị sẽ thờ phượng Cha không phải trên núi này, cũng không phải tại Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với chị ấy: "Chị ơi, hãy tin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Sắp đến lúc chị và dân tộc chị sẽ thờ phượng Cha, nhưng không phải trên núi này, cũng không phải ở Giê-ru-sa-lem.

decisions.choice: an hour is coming: the time God has set, which begins with Jesus
decisions.reason: As with Jesus's hour (2:4), this is a time set by God. Verse 23 adds "and now is": with Jesus it has already begun. His body is the new temple (2:19-21), so worship will no longer be bound to a place.

decisions.choice: Woman: a respectful address
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:4. Jesus speaks to her with the same courtesy he shows his mother.

decisions.choice: you will worship: plural, the woman and her people
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. Jesus speaks of a time when her people will worship the Father, neither at Gerizim nor at Jerusalem but in the way verses 23-24 describe. Verses 39-42 begin to fulfil it.

decisions.choice: the Father: Jesus speaks of God as Father
decisions.reason: From here to verse 23 Jesus calls God "the Father": true worship is worship of the Father whom the Son makes known (1:18).

decisions.choice: believe me: trust what I say
decisions.reason: With a plain object rather than "in", the verb means to accept what someone says as true.

decisions.choice: Woman
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: "Woman" on its own can sound cold, but keeping it lets readers connect the passages; the footnote says it was respectful.

decisions.choice: Dear woman
decisions.reason: For young readers "Woman" sounds rude, which the Greek is not; "Dear woman" keeps the courtesy (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: A time
decisions.reason: "Hour" sounds like sixty minutes; Literal and Balanced keep "hour" so the thread through the Gospel stays visible.

decisions.choice: you [all] (L); your worship (B); you and your people (R)
decisions.reason: Shows that "you" is plural (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: your worship of the Father will not be on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem either
alternatives: you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Natural word order that keeps the stress on the two places.

decisions.choice: mujer at every level
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the Greek address is respectful (meaning decision m2). Spanish "mujer" as an address is less cold than English "Woman", so Readable keeps it too and readers can connect the passages; the footnote says it was courteous.

decisions.choice: hora at every level
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: Spanish "llega la hora" is everyday language for an appointed time.

decisions.choice: tú y tu pueblo
decisions.reason: The Spanish verb already shows the plural (meaning decision m3), so Literal and Balanced need no added word; Readable says who is meant.

decisions.choice: Mama at every level
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: γύναι is respectful in Greek, and "Mwanamke!" said to a woman's face is rude in Swahili. "Mama" is the respectful address to any grown woman, not only one's mother.

decisions.choice: hamtamwabudu: the plural is in the verb
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to her but says "you" in the plural, meaning her people. Swahili marks the plural in the verb (ham-), so Literal needs no bracketed "[all]".

decisions.choice: "여자여" (L); "여인이여" (B); "부인" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek address is respectful. Literal keeps the word; Balanced uses the more courteous "여인이여" as the guide sets, and Readable "부인", the ordinary polite way to address a grown woman.

decisions.choice: "때" for "hour" at every level
decisions.reason: Korean "때" means both "hour" in John's sense, the appointed time, and plain "time", so one word keeps the thread at all three levels. The plural of "you will worship" is in "너희", with nothing in brackets.

decisions.choice: "hỡi chị" (L); "Này chị" (B); "Chị ơi" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek address "Woman" is respectful; Vietnamese "đàn bà" as a form of address would sound rude, so the kin term already used in the scene carries it.

decisions.choice: "các người" (L); "dân chị" (B); "chị và dân tộc chị" (R) for the plural "you"; likewise in 4:22
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "chị" is singular; the plural must be shown. "các chị" would mean a group of women, so Literal uses the general plural "các người" and the other levels name her people.

source.text: ὑμεῖς προσκυνεῖτε ὃ οὐκ οἴδατε, ἡμεῖς προσκυνοῦμεν ὃ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι ἡ σωτηρία ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐστίν·

records.literal_gloss: You worship what not you know; we worship what we know, because the salvation from the Jews is;

en.L: You [all] worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
en.B: Your people worship without knowing what they worship; we know what we worship, since salvation comes from the Jews.
en.R: You Samaritans do not really know the God you worship. We Jews know the God we worship, because God's salvation comes from the Jewish people.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes adoran lo que no conocen|Vosotros adoráis lo que no conocéis}}; nosotros adoramos lo que conocemos, porque la salvación viene de los judíos.
es.B: Tu pueblo adora sin saber lo que adora; nosotros sabemos lo que adoramos, porque la salvación viene de los judíos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes los samaritanos no conocen de verdad al Dios que adoran|Vosotros los samaritanos no conocéis de verdad al Dios que adoráis}}. Nosotros los judíos sí conocemos al Dios que adoramos, porque la salvación de Dios viene del pueblo judío.

sw.L: Ninyi mnaabudu kile msichokijua; sisi tunaabudu kile tunachokijua, kwa kuwa wokovu ni kutoka kwa Wayahudi.
sw.B: Watu wenu wanaabudu bila kujua wanachokiabudu; sisi tunajua tunachokiabudu, kwa kuwa wokovu unatoka kwa Wayahudi.
sw.R: Ninyi Wasamaria hammjui kwa kweli Mungu mnayemwabudu. Sisi Wayahudi tunamjua Mungu tunayemwabudu, kwa sababu wokovu wa Mungu unakuja kupitia watu wa Kiyahudi.

ko.L: 너희는 알지 못하는 것을 예배하고, 우리는 아는 것을 예배한다. 구원은 유대인들에게서 나오기 때문이다.
ko.B: 너희는 무엇을 예배하는지 모르고 예배하지만, 우리는 우리가 예배하는 분을 안다. 구원이 유대인들에게서 나오기 때문이다.
ko.R: 너희 사마리아 사람들은 너희가 예배하는 하나님을 잘 알지 못한다. 우리 유대인들은 우리가 예배하는 하나님을 안다. 하나님의 구원이 유대 민족에게서 나오기 때문이다.

vi.L: Các người thờ phượng điều các người không biết; chúng tôi thờ phượng điều chúng tôi biết, vì sự cứu rỗi đến từ người Do Thái.
vi.B: Dân chị thờ phượng mà không biết mình thờ phượng điều gì; còn chúng tôi biết điều mình thờ phượng, vì sự cứu rỗi đến từ người Do Thái.
vi.R: Người Sa-ma-ri các chị không thật sự biết Đấng mình thờ phượng. Người Do Thái chúng tôi biết Đấng mình thờ phượng, vì sự cứu rỗi của Đức Chúa Trời đến qua dân Do Thái.

decisions.choice: you (plural): the Samaritans; we: the Jews, among whom Jesus counts himself
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks as a Jew to a Samaritan, taking up her "our fathers" and "you" (verse 20).

decisions.choice: what: worship that does not truly know its object
decisions.reason: The neuter "what" rather than "whom" suggests worship without full knowledge of the God it is offered to. The Samaritans accepted the books of Moses but not the Prophets, and 2 Kings 17:33 describes the settlers as fearing the LORD while serving their own gods. Jesus's "we know" rests on what God made known to Israel.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people
decisions.reason: Here the word clearly means the Jewish people, and Jesus speaks as one of them.

decisions.choice: salvation is from the Jews: God's saving work comes through Israel
decisions.reason: God's promises were given to Israel for all nations (Genesis 12:3; Isaiah 2:3), and the Christ comes from Israel by descent (Romans 9:4-5). The Samaritans of Sychar will call Jesus "the Savior of the world" (verse 42).

decisions.choice: Your people (B); You Samaritans, We Jews (R)
decisions.reason: Shows who "you" and "we" are (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the Jewish people
decisions.reason: The word means the people here (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: the God you worship; the God we worship
decisions.reason: Readable names the one worshiped; "not really" keeps the sense of the neuter (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Tu pueblo (B); ustedes los samaritanos, nosotros los judíos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: shows who "you" and "we" are (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: al Dios que adoran
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the one worshiped; "no ... de verdad" keeps the sense of the neuter (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" (we, not including the hearer)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks as one of the Jews over against the Samaritans; the exclusive "chúng tôi" shows that, and that he counts himself a Jew.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν, ὅτε οἱ ἀληθινοὶ προσκυνηταὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ πατρὶ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, καὶ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ τοιούτους ζητεῖ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: But is coming an hour and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for also the Father such seeks the ones worshiping him;

en.L: But an hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for indeed the Father seeks such [{{gender:people|men}}] as those who worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: But an hour is coming, and in fact it has already begun, when true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking {{gender:people|men}} like these to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But a time is coming, and it has already started, when those who truly worship the Father will worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in spirit and in truth. The Father is looking for {{gender:people|men}} who will worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like that.

es.L: Pero viene una hora, y ahora es, cuando los verdaderos adoradores adorarán al Padre en espíritu y verdad; porque también el Padre busca a tales que lo adoren.
es.B: Pero viene una hora, y de hecho ya ha llegado, en que los verdaderos adoradores adorarán al Padre en espíritu y en verdad; porque el Padre busca que así sean los que lo adoran.
es.R: Pero llega la hora, y ya ha comenzado, en que los que adoran de verdad al Padre lo adorarán en espíritu y en verdad. El Padre busca personas que lo adoren así.

sw.L: Lakini saa inakuja, na sasa imefika, ambapo waabudu wa kweli watamwabudu Baba katika roho na kweli; kwa maana kweli Baba anatafuta watu wa aina hiyo wawe waabudu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Lakini saa inakuja, na kwa hakika imekwisha anza, ambapo waabudu wa kweli watamwabudu Baba katika roho na kweli; kwa maana Baba anatafuta watu kama hao wamwabudu.
sw.R: Lakini wakati unakuja, na umekwisha anza, ambapo wale wanaomwabudu Baba kwa kweli watamwabudu katika roho na katika kweli. Baba anatafuta watu watakaomwabudu namna hiyo.

ko.L: 그러나 때가 오는데, 지금이 바로 그때이다. 그때에는 참된 예배자들이 영과 진리로 아버지께 예배할 것이다. 참으로 아버지께서는 그러한 [사람들을] 자신에게 예배하는 사람들로 찾으신다.
ko.B: 그러나 참된 예배자들이 영과 진리로 아버지께 예배할 때가 오는데, 바로 지금이 그때이다. 아버지께서는 이렇게 예배하는 사람들을 찾고 계신다.
ko.R: 그러나 때가 오고 있다. 아니, 벌써 그때가 시작되었다. 그때에는 아버지께 참되게 예배하는 사람들이 영과 진리로 그분께 예배할 것이다. 아버지께서는 그렇게 예배할 사람들을 찾고 계신다.

vi.L: Nhưng giờ đang đến, và nay đã đến rồi, khi những người thờ phượng thật sẽ thờ phượng Cha trong tâm linh và chân lý; vì Cha cũng tìm kiếm những người như thế làm người thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Nhưng giờ đang đến, và thật ra đã đến rồi, khi những người thờ phượng thật sẽ thờ phượng Cha trong tâm linh và chân lý; vì Cha đang tìm những người như vậy để thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Nhưng sắp đến lúc, và thật ra lúc ấy đã bắt đầu rồi, những người thật lòng thờ phượng Cha sẽ thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bằng cả tâm linh và chân lý. Cha đang tìm những người thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như thế.

decisions.choice: is coming and now is: the future time is already present in Jesus
decisions.reason: The hour still lies ahead, but with Jesus present it has already begun. John says the same of the hour when the dead hear the voice of the Son of God (5:25).

decisions.choice: true: genuine, real
decisions.reason: ἀληθινοὶ means real or genuine, as in "the true light" (1:9) and "the true vine" (15:1).

decisions.choice: in spirit and truth: one idea, worship that fits who God is (spirit, verse 24) and the truth he has made known; spirit is not capitalized
alternatives: in the Spirit and in truth: worship given through the Holy Spirit
in one's inner spirit, sincerely, as against outward ritual
decisions.reason: One preposition governs both nouns, so they form a single idea. Verse 24 grounds it: God is spirit, so worship must be "in spirit". The word could refer to the Holy Spirit, whom John links with new birth (3:5-8) and calls "the Spirit of truth" (14:17; 15:26), and through whom such worship becomes possible. But the sentence describes the kind of worship rather than naming the Spirit, and verse 24 uses the same word of God's own being, so it is not capitalized here. It is not mere inward sincerity either, since it is joined to truth. The evidence is balanced; the footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: truth: the reality of God made known in Jesus
decisions.reason: In John truth is God's reality made known: grace and truth came through Jesus Christ (1:17), and he is the truth (14:6). True worship is shaped by that truth, not only offered sincerely.

decisions.choice: the Father seeks such people as his worshipers: God takes the first step
decisions.reason: Word for word, "the Father seeks such [people as] those who worship him": the participle says what he seeks them to be. The masculine is general and includes men and women. Worship begins with God's seeking, as the shepherd seeks the lost (Ezekiel 34:11-12; Luke 19:10); at the well Jesus has been doing just that.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: Men and women are meant; inclusive by default, the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: it has already begun (B); it has already started (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for the hour's present arrival (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: a time
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish can say "a tales", "los que lo adoran" or "personas", all general, so no setting is needed (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: en espíritu y (en) verdad, "espíritu" in lower case
decisions.reason: As meaning decision m3 says, the phrase is one idea and "espíritu" is not capitalized; its footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: "영과 진리로", with "영", not "성령"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "spirit" here as worship that fits who God is, not the Holy Spirit, so Korean uses "영" as the guide does for 4:24. The traditional "신령과 진정으로" is an older Korean phrasing and is not used.

decisions.choice: "trong tâm linh và chân lý"
decisions.reason: "tâm linh" is the spirit, lowercase, not the Holy Spirit; it shares "linh" with "thần linh" in 4:24, though less plainly than the Greek, which uses one word. "chân lý" is the book's key term for truth.

decisions.choice: God is spirit: what God is, not "a spirit" and not the Holy Spirit
alternatives: God is a spirit, one among many
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα stands first without the article and describes God's nature, like "God is light" (1 John 1:5) and "God is love" (1 John 4:8). God is not bound to a body or a place, so he cannot be confined to one mountain or one city (compare 1 Kings 8:27). Since it describes God's being and does not name the Holy Spirit, the book-wide choice is not to capitalize it.

decisions.choice: must: a necessity that comes from who God is
decisions.reason: The woman spoke of the place where people "must" worship (verse 20). Jesus answers with a "must" that rests on God's own nature, not on a place.

decisions.choice: in spirit and truth: as in verse 23
alternatives: in the Spirit and in truth
decisions.reason: See meaning decision m3 at verse 23, whose footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: those who worship him: men and women alike
decisions.reason: The masculine plural participle is general.

decisions.choice: it is necessary for those who worship him to worship
alternatives: those who worship him must worship
decisions.reason: Keeps the Greek shape, with the necessity stated before the worship it governs.

decisions.choice: anyone who worships him (B); when people worship him (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words that include men and women without needing the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Mungu ni roho, lowercase
decisions.reason: The meaning note says this is what God is, not the Holy Spirit. Swahili writes "Roho" with a capital for the Holy Spirit, so here, and in "katika roho na kweli", it is lowercase, as the English has "spirit".

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời là thần linh", lowercase
decisions.reason: What God is, not the Holy Spirit; the style guide keeps lowercase "thần linh" here.

vi.B: Người phụ nữ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tôi biết Đấng Mê-si-a sẽ đến" (cũng gọi là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Được Xức Dầu}}). "Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ giải bày mọi điều cho chúng tôi."

decisions.choice: Messiah: the Hebrew title in Greek letters, which John translates
decisions.reason: As at 1:41, the word Μεσσίας is the Hebrew (and Aramaic) title, anointed one, written in Greek letters and then translated with χριστός. The woman uses it without the article, almost as a name.

decisions.choice: who is called Christ: most likely the narrator's explanation
decisions.reason: At 1:38, 1:41 and 1:42 John stops to translate a Hebrew or Aramaic word for his readers, and this phrase does the same, so it is set outside her words. The manuscripts have no quotation marks, though, and the words can be read as hers.

decisions.choice: the Samaritan hope: a coming one who would teach the truth
decisions.reason: The Samaritans drew their hope from the five books of Moses, especially the prophet like Moses who would tell the people all that God commanded (Deuteronomy 18:18). Her words "he will declare all things to us" fit that hope. Later Samaritan writings call the coming one the Taheb, "the one who returns"; how much of that belief goes back to Jesus's day is not certain.

decisions.choice: declare: make known, report
decisions.reason: She expects the coming one to settle questions like the one she raised about worship (verse 20). The same verb is used of the Spirit, who "will declare" to the disciples what is to come (16:13-15).

decisions.choice: Messiah, plain; {{christos:Christ|Anointed One}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for 1:41 and 4:25: Messiah is the woman's word and is written plainly. The christos setting is on the explanation only, with "Anointed One" as its alternative, so no setting can produce "Messiah (who is called Messiah)".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} for the coming one
decisions.reason: The one she speaks of is Christ, so the pronouns for him take the setting, though she does not yet know who he is. Literal brackets the "he" that the verb contains.

decisions.choice: Messiah means the Anointed One, the one God promised to send
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title (meaning decisions m1 and m3) without making it the king of David's line, which was the Jewish rather than the Samaritan hope.

decisions.choice: make everything plain (B); explain everything (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for what she expects (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Mesías, plain; {{christos:Cristo|Ungido}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for 1:41 and 4:25: "Mesías" is the woman's word and is written plainly; the setting is on the explanation only. Spanish needs the article ("[el] Mesías" at Literal).

decisions.choice: no pronoun for the coming one
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ("cuando venga"), so no deity_pronoun span is needed; Literal keeps the demonstrative "aquel".

decisions.choice: Masihi, plain; {{christos:Kristo|Aliyetiwa Mafuta}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: As at 1:41: the Hebrew title is written plainly and the explanation has its own alternative, so no setting can produce "Masihi (who is called Masihi)".

decisions.choice: "메시아", plain; {{christos:그리스도|기름 부음 받은 이}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: The guide's usual alternative is "메시아", which here would produce "Messiah (who is called Messiah)". As john-terms.md asks, the explanation gets its own alternative, "기름 부음 받은 이" (the Anointed One).

decisions.choice: "Đấng Mê-si-a" plain; {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Được Xức Dầu}} for the explanation
decisions.reason: The book's usual christos alternative is "Đấng Mê-si-a", which here would read "the Messiah ... called the Messiah"; as docs/john-terms.md asks, the explanation gets its own alternative, "the Anointed One".

decisions.choice: I am: plainly "I am he", the Messiah, with a possible echo of God's own words
alternatives: the divine name, I AM, as the main sense
only the plain sense, with no echo
decisions.reason: The words Ἐγώ εἰμι have no predicate, but the woman has just spoken of Messiah, so the plain sense is "I am he": Jesus says openly what he is, as he does to no one else so plainly before his trial (compare 10:24-25). The same words are how God speaks of himself in the Greek of Isaiah (43:10; 46:4), and in Isaiah 52:6 God says, "I am he who is speaking", very like the wording here. Later in John the bare "I am" carries that echo more clearly (8:24, 28, 58). Here the plain sense is uppermost and the echo possible, so the decision is marked uncertain.

decisions.choice: the one speaking to you: the one she awaits is already here
decisions.reason: She spoke of one who will come and declare all things; the one now declaring things to her is he. The conversation that began with his request for water ends with his naming himself.

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L); I am he (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "I am". Literal brackets the "he" the sentence needs; Balanced writes it. As a pronoun for Christ it takes the deity_pronoun setting. The footnote gives the bare words, so the echo noted in meaning decision m1 stays visible.

decisions.choice: I am the Messiah
decisions.reason: Readable says whom "he" refers to (verse 25).

decisions.choice: Yo soy, with no supplied pronoun (L, B)
decisions.reason: In Spanish "Yo soy" is a complete answer ("I am the one"), so Literal and Balanced need no added "he", and the possible echo of God's own words (meaning decision m1) stays as it is in the Greek. The footnote gives the echo.

decisions.choice: Yo soy el Mesías
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says whom "I am" refers to (verse 25).

decisions.choice: Mimi ndiye
decisions.reason: "Ndiye" (I am the one) is the ordinary Swahili for "I am he", so Literal needs no bracket where the English has "I am [he]". It leaves open the echo of God's name that the meaning note mentions.

decisions.choice: "너에게 말하고 있는 내가 [그]이다": "the one speaking to you" placed before "I am"
decisions.reason: Korean puts the describing phrase before "I" and the verb last, so the Greek apposition becomes one clause. The bare "I am" is completed by "그" (he), in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: "Đấng ấy"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a complement after "là"; "Đấng" is the respectful classifier she used for the Messiah.
